messages.subject: BSM errors
parts:
Hi,

I’m running BioGeoBEARS and 100 BSMs on a rapid radiation of ~100 species endemic to New Zealand, time-stratified based very roughly on phases of uplift in the southern Alps (lowland, subalpine, and alpine zones). The best model for this tree by AIC was BAYAREA+J, which is what I’m using for the BSMS. Although I’m getting seemingly successful output for all the mappings, I’m getting several errors and warnings, and am not sure how critical they are.

 For a handful of nodes, I get this error for most mappings:

```

Error_in_stochastic_simulation; no success on branch below node 74 after 40000 tries. Printing starting/ending states, and events table for last attempt.

 Starting state (1-based): 7

 Ending state (1-based): 7

Goal state (1-based): 2

 [1] "Last attempt at events_table_for_branch:"

       [,1] [,2]    [,3]  [,4] [,5] [,6] [,7] [,8]             

tmprow "49" "40001" "2.1" "4"  "7"  "L"  "SL" "3.4903741724477"

tmprow "49" "40001" "2.1" "7"  "4"  "SL" "L"  "3.34332238278415"

tmprow "49" "40001" "2.1" "4"  "7"  "L"  "SL" "2.93741075091836"

       [,9]                [,10] [,11]   [,12] [,13] [,14] [,15]

tmprow "0.509625827552303" "d"   "L->SL" "2"   "-"   "S"   "-" 

tmprow "0.65667761721585"  "e"   "SL->L" "-"   "2"   "-"   "S" 

tmprow "1.06258924908164"  "d"   "L->SL" "2"   "-"   "S"   "-" 

 ```

Based on the node numbers,  these errors all appear to be for long terminal branches that cross the stratifications, forcing the mapping to switch ranges to get to a current range that wasn’t allowed in the ancestral node (e.g. ancestral lowland before any uplift to current alpine).  Not sure how important this is, but the areas printed out don’t always match what I expect to see—the above example says the starting state is 7, which corresponds to “SL” while the parent node of node 79 is “L”. Is this because it’s starting from the middle of the branch? (I don't totally follow the table so maybe it's obvious.) 

 

This is always followed by this error for a different node (but the same few throughout the mappings):

```

Error in stochastic_map_branch(): Stochastic mapping failed after maxtries=40000 tries on branch below node=50

As manual_history_for_difficult_branches==TRUE, we are manually devising a history to force-fit a difficult branch (e.g. AB -> ACEDFGH)...

NOTE: This fix will run, but will NOT work correctly for pure '+a' models (as of 2016-05-07) where d and/or e equals 0, since the manual fix forces a random series of d and e events, on the theory that the events must be super-rare since maxtries failed, so we might as well order them randomly (subject to the constraint that the range is never NULL). For +a models, try increasing maxtries instead.

Starting range:  L

Desired ending range:  ASL

 ```

For most of the these errors, the nodes listed are relatively short terminal branches with no observable problem in the ranges and definitely not matching the starting and desired end range, so I’m quite confused about that—the above example is a terminal node with range AS from an ancestral node AS in the consensus tree. I must be missing something.

 

Finally, at the end, I get this warning (for various area combinations) over 21,000 times, which is far more than the above errors so I’m not sure if it’s related:

 ```

simulate_source_area_ana() says: WARNING: the sum of source_area_relprob2 is 0. This means that all possible source areas have probability zero. In stochastic mapping, this could happen if, e.g. in a time-stratified stochastic map, the simulated state at the top of the previous time-bin is an impossible starting range for the manual history in the current time bin. In this situation, the 'manual history' option probably forced a history, just to stop you from running millions of tries pointlessly. This is part of the overall problem with very-improbable histories in stochastic mapping with huge biogeographical state spaces and complex modifications and lots of constratints.  If you get this warning, you should (a) be grateful that this code works at all, programming all of this is ridiculously complex, especially in R, and (b) you should probably delete these histories from your collection, if you can, although the overall effect should be minor.  Here, we are re-setting source_area_relprob2 to source_area_relprob2=rep(1, times=length(source_area_relprob2)). The events_txt being tried here was: 'L->SL'.

 ```

I don’t see that deleting histories is an option, since the warning happens so many times and I also can’t tell exactly when it’s happening.

 

Is there some way I can address these errors/warnings, or does it sound like it’s just the nature of my dataset (e.g. long branches crossing time stratifications)? Can they be ignored given that I'm getting output or is this problematic? 

 

Thanks very much,

Anne Thomas

messages.author: 115d05260b0c341a
messages.subject: Re: [BioGeoBEARS] Re: BSM errors
parts:
Hi -- sorry for the slow reply.  Those error messages, which as you can see are quite elaborate, are my best guess about the kinds of things that are probably happening. Getting successful simulations gets more and more challenging as more and more constraints get piled on, especially with areas appearing/disappearing through time, short sub-branches resulting from time-stratification chopping up the branches, etc.  Keep in mind that BSM is trying to simulate histories on branches *by chance* that match the (also simulated) state at the top of the branch.  This gets particularly challenging when various multiple-area ranges are involved.  For a particular branch, it will try 40,000 times (by default) and then give up.

If you got some successful simulations out of it, the simplest thing is to just go with those and ignore the rest.  Probably this is 99.9% of what you need. 

By deleting histories, I just meant that the results have a bunch of tables, each representing a history, and you remove the ones that didn't work.

If the problems are more severe, ie you have no valid histories, then probably the best bet is to simplify the problem (reduce the number of areas or the constraints) and try again.

A simpler strategy is to up maxtries from 40000 to 1 million or something, but this only gives you 20times more tries, so it will only help on moderately difficult problems.

Since your model is basically BAYAREALIKE anyways, actually the "manual_history_for_difficult_branches==TRUE, we are manually devising a history to force-fit a difficult branch (e.g. AB -> ACEDFGH)" is totally fine as it is using the BAYAREALIKE process (a series of range additions and subtractions) to divise a history

Happy to work more with you on email if none of this helps,

Cheers,
Nick

Hi Nick,

Thanks very much for your reply and no worries. I'm still trying to wrap my head around the relationship between these functions and their warnings, and whether I'm getting successful simulations in spite of them. I realized that the "simulation_source_ana" function and warnings come later in the example script, not from run_BSM itself, unlike the stochastic_simulation and stochastic_branch_map() errors. Are they likely connected, or are they separate issues? 

I wonder because, at the moment, my goal with the BSMs is to bin cladogenetic events (at nodes) in the different areas over time, with a similar approach to Igea and Tanentzap 2019 (https://advances.sciencemag.org/content/5/2/eaau8067, in turn modeled after Xing and Ree 2017). We've actually only been working with the direct output of run_BSM without the additions of simulation_source_ana_clado(). As I very superficially understand it, this pinpoints a particular source area when the ancestor was widespread, so if I'm not concerned about this, is it valid to go without the function altogether? 

If the earlier stochastic_map errors are the main issue regardless of this, I want to clarify what I should be looking for--when you say "some successful simulations" do you mean each overall stochastic mapping? I'm getting "Success #n/100 on stochastic mapping attempt #n/100 tries" for all the mappings, so is this good enough evidence that I can move forward with it as is? Especially given what you said about manual_history_for_difficult_branches and BAYAREALIKE being fine.

If running  simulation_source_ana_clado() is necessary, I'm also getting event count tables out of that, but I'm not sure how to determine if they're complete/if this is what you're talking about. Which tables represent the histories? (Or do I not need to worry about this?)

Thanks for your patience with my inexperienced questions!

Best,
Anne

Hi -- sorry for the slow reply.  Those error messages, which as you can see are quite elaborate, are my best guess about the kinds of things that are probably happening. Getting successful simulations gets more and more challenging as more and more constraints get piled on, especially with areas appearing/disappearing through time, short sub-branches resulting from time-stratification chopping up the branches, etc.  Keep in mind that BSM is trying to simulate histories on branches *by chance* that match the (also simulated) state at the top of the branch.  This gets particularly challenging when various multiple-area ranges are involved.  For a particular branch, it will try 40,000 times (by default) and then give up.

If you got some successful simulations out of it, the simplest thing is to just go with those and ignore the rest.  Probably this is 99.9% of what you need. 

By deleting histories, I just meant that the results have a bunch of tables, each representing a history, and you remove the ones that didn't work.

If the problems are more severe, ie you have no valid histories, then probably the best bet is to simplify the problem (reduce the number of areas or the constraints) and try again.

A simpler strategy is to up maxtries from 40000 to 1 million or something, but this only gives you 20times more tries, so it will only help on moderately difficult problems.

Since your model is basically BAYAREALIKE anyways, actually the "manual_history_for_difficult_branches==TRUE, we are manually devising a history to force-fit a difficult branch (e.g. AB -> ACEDFGH)" is totally fine as it is using the BAYAREALIKE process (a series of range additions and subtractions) to divise a history

Happy to work more with you on email if none of this helps,

Cheers,
Nick
